title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE 9
alt_titles: NEUROPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE 9

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE 9

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the COQ7 gene (601683) on chromosome 16p12.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the COQ7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we have identified the first example of recessive distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by a homozygous variation in the COQ7 gene
checks.explanation: The paper reports only a homozygous COQ7 mutation in one family. It does not report compound heterozygous mutations causing dHMN, and it does not use the HMNR9 designation.

checks.claim: The COQ7 gene is located on chromosome 16p12.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with the identification of a homozygous mutation in the COQ7 gene located on chromosome 16
checks.explanation: The paper places COQ7 on chromosome 16. The 16p12 band is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is a neurologic disorder. Affected individuals have slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs, because of a length-dependent loss of motor nerve function. Sensory involvement is absent or minimal. Some patients also have upper motor neuron signs. Unlike the more severe multisystem primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency caused by other COQ7 mutations, the disorder is mostly limited to the peripheral motor system.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is a neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) is a motor inherited neuropathy, resulting in a distal weakness starting in the lower limbs, with a slowly progressive course.
checks.explanation: The paper describes dHMN as an inherited motor neuropathy, which is a neurologic disorder.

checks.claim: Individuals with HMNR9 have slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle weakness worsened gradually with a predominance in the distal part of the lower limbs (Fig. 1B). At the age of 32 years, he developed muscle weakness in the hands
checks.explanation: The patients had slowly progressive distal weakness, and the paper reports amyotrophy (muscle wasting) in the lower limbs and hands.

checks.claim: The distal weakness and atrophy in HMNR9 mainly affect the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: There was evidence of a pure motor axonal neuropathy predominantly affecting the distal part of the lower limbs.
checks.explanation: The weakness predominantly affected the distal lower limbs.

checks.claim: The distal weakness and atrophy in HMNR9 result from a length-dependent loss of motor nerve function.
checks.evidence_quote: All of the patients presented with length-dependent pure motor axonal neuropathy, leading to progressive walking difficulties and disability, with childhood onset.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a length-dependent motor axonal neuropathy.

checks.claim: Sensory involvement in HMNR9 is absent or minimal.
checks.evidence_quote: He had never complained of sensory symptoms.
checks.explanation: Sensory examination was normal in all three patients. One patient reported trouble feeling temperature in her feet, which fits 'absent or minimal'.

checks.claim: Some patients with HMNR9 have upper motor neuron signs.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical phenotype of dHMN with pyramidal features reported here is suggestive of upper motor neuron involvement.
checks.explanation: Patients had brisk reflexes, a Hoffman sign or a Babinski sign.

checks.claim: HMNR9 is mostly limited to the peripheral motor system.
checks.evidence_quote: the family studied here presented with a less severe phenotype characterized by isolated neurological damage of motor neurons, despite comprehensive systemic explorations.
checks.explanation: The disorder was restricted to motor neurons.

checks.claim: Other COQ7 mutations cause a more severe, multisystem primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations of COQ7 were previously associated with primary CoQ10 deficiencies (MIM 601683, COQ10D8) encompassing a large spectrum of severe phenotypes.
checks.explanation: The abstract also describes these as severe multi-organ disorders.

paragraphs.text: Rebelo et al. (2023) reported patients from several unrelated families with distal hereditary motor neuropathy. Distal weakness and wasting began in childhood or adolescence and mainly affected the lower limbs. Some patients also had upper motor neuron signs. Electrophysiologic studies showed a motor axonal neuropathy with little or no sensory involvement.

checks.claim: Rebelo et al. (2023) reported patients with distal hereditary motor neuropathy from several unrelated families.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This paper is Jacquier et al. (2023) and reports a single Portuguese family. It does not describe Rebelo et al. (2023) or several unrelated families.

checks.claim: In the patients with distal hereditary motor neuropathy reported by Rebelo et al. (2023), distal weakness and wasting began in childhood or adolescence.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The claim concerns patients reported by Rebelo et al., who are not in this paper. Jacquier et al. report onset at ages 9 to 12 years in their own family.

checks.claim: In the patients with distal hereditary motor neuropathy reported by Rebelo et al. (2023), distal weakness and wasting mainly affected the lower limbs.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The claim concerns Rebelo et al.'s patients, who are not described here. This paper reports lower-limb predominance only in its own family.

checks.claim: Some of the patients with distal hereditary motor neuropathy reported by Rebelo et al. (2023) had upper motor neuron signs.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The claim concerns Rebelo et al.'s patients, who are not described here. This paper reports pyramidal signs only in its own family.

checks.claim: Electrophysiologic studies in the patients reported by Rebelo et al. (2023) showed a motor axonal neuropathy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The claim concerns Rebelo et al.'s patients, who are not described here. ENMG in this paper covers only the authors' own family.

checks.claim: Electrophysiologic studies in the patients reported by Rebelo et al. (2023) showed little or no sensory involvement.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The claim concerns Rebelo et al.'s patients, who are not described here.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of HMNR9 in the families reported by Rebelo et al. (2023) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of HMNR9 in the families reported by Rebelo et al. (2023) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This paper does not report Rebelo et al.'s families. It does describe an autosomal recessive pattern, but only in its own single family.

paragraphs.text: Other COQ7 mutations cause primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency. That disorder is more severe and multisystemic, and can include neonatal-onset disease, developmental delay, spasticity and hearing loss. HMNR9 is therefore allelic to it.

checks.claim: Other COQ7 mutations cause primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations of COQ7 were previously associated with primary CoQ10 deficiencies (MIM 601683, COQ10D8)
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency caused by COQ7 mutation is more severe and multisystemic than HMNR9.
checks.evidence_quote: Compared to previously reported patients with COQ7 mutations, the family studied here presented with a less severe phenotype characterized by isolated neurological damage of motor neurons
checks.explanation: Earlier COQ7 cases were more severe, and the abstract calls them multi-organ disorders.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency caused by COQ7 mutation can include neonatal-onset disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Kwong et al. described another patient presenting with multiorgan failure at birth harbouring a compound heterozygous mutation in COQ7.
checks.explanation: The paper reports onset at birth in previously described cases.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency caused by COQ7 mutation can include developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: Six families of patients with early childhood onsets and developmental delays were identified.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency caused by COQ7 mutation can include spasticity.
checks.evidence_quote: Wang et al. and Hashemi et al. extended the phenotype of COQ7-associated diseases by reporting two patients affected by hereditary spastic paraplegia associated with developmental delay.
checks.explanation: Spastic paraplegia implies spasticity.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency caused by COQ7 mutation can include hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: While COQ7 has been associated with hearing loss in past reports,,, hearing loss did not segregate with COQ7 variants in this report.
checks.explanation: Hearing loss associated with COQ7 in prior reports.

checks.claim: HMNR9 is allelic to COQ7-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we extend the spectrum of COQ7-associated disorders by reporting the first familial cases of patients affected by COQ7 mutation and presenting with a pure distal motor neuropathy.
checks.explanation: Both disorders arise from mutations in the same gene, so they are allelic.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of families with distal hereditary motor neuropathy, Rebelo et al. (2023) identified biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) mutations in the COQ7 gene. COQ7 encodes an enzyme in the biosynthesis of coenzyme Q10. Functional studies showed reduced COQ7 function and disturbed CoQ10 biosynthesis.

checks.claim: Rebelo et al. (2023) identified biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) COQ7 mutations in affected members of families with distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. This paper does not report Rebelo et al.'s findings. It describes only a homozygous c.3G>T variant in one family and no compound heterozygous dHMN cases.

checks.claim: COQ7 encodes an enzyme in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: By catalysing the hydroxylation of 6-DMQ in mitochondria, COQ7 is one of the main enzymes involved in CoQ10 synthesis.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Functional studies of the COQ7 mutations identified by Rebelo et al. (2023) showed reduced COQ7 function.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The claim concerns Rebelo et al.'s mutations, which this paper does not study. Its functional work covers only its own c.3G>T variant.

checks.claim: Functional studies of the COQ7 mutations identified by Rebelo et al. (2023) showed disturbed coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 4 cited papers. The claim concerns Rebelo et al.'s mutations. The CoQ10 findings in this paper apply only to its own c.3G>T variant.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Upper motor neuron signs in some patients
